title: Lead intake & CRM sync
description: An n8n workflow that takes a lead from any form, cleans it, de-duplicates it, tells sales and replies to the prospect, in one execution. Built by Dyaksa.
intro: An n8n workflow that takes a lead from any form, cleans it, checks it isn't already in the CRM, tells sales and replies to the prospect, all in one execution. Scroll to follow one lead through all 14 nodes.

stations.title: One door for every form.
stations.body: The website form, campaign landing pages and partner APIs all POST to one webhook. They don't agree on field names.

stations.title: Make every lead look the same.
stations.body: A Code node maps field-name variants to one schema, trims and lower-cases the email, and checks it before anything is written.

stations.title: Bad input never reaches the CRM.
stations.body: An invalid lead goes to a Rejected Submissions sheet, and the form gets a 400 with the reason. Nothing disappears, and nothing dirty gets written.

stations.title: Same person twice is still one contact.
stations.body: The lookup keys on email. Always Output Data is on, so a lead with no match still reaches the IF and takes the create branch instead of quietly ending the run. A repeat updates lastTouchedAt and bumps touchCount.

stations.title: Sales hears about it straight away.
stations.body: The row is written, then Slack. Every node after an API call reads the lead from the Code node, because an API node's output is its response, not the lead.
check: Create New CRM Row → Notify Sales

stations.title: The prospect gets a reply. The form gets an answer.
stations.body: A confirmation email goes out, then Respond to Webhook returns 200 with JSON in the same execution, so the form can show the right message.

stations.title: When the workflow itself fails, someone hears.
stations.body: An Error Trigger catches any failed execution and posts it to #eng-alerts. The lead can still be recovered from n8n's execution history. A dropped lead nobody notices is the exact problem this workflow exists to prevent.

stations.title: 14 nodes, one execution.
stations.body: Every outcome, whether new, duplicate, invalid or failed, ends in a log row or an alert. The CRM is a Google Sheet on purpose: swapping in HubSpot or Pipedrive changes the sink, not the graph.
